title: Norm sections of powers of a pulled-back invertible module
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be a finite locally free morphism of schemes of constant degree $d\geq1$ [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], let $n\geq1$, and let $s\in\Gamma(Y,(f^*L)^{\otimes n})$, where tensor pullback is [def-pc-module-pullback] and tensor powers and nonvanishing opens are [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. There is a section $t\in\Gamma(X,L^{\otimes(dn)})$ such that $$X_t=\{x\in X:\ f^{-1}(\{x\})\subseteq Y_s\}=X\setminus f(Y\setminus Y_s).$$ No ampleness, properness, normality, Noetherianity, reducedness or separability hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tags 0BD2 (divisors-lemma-finite-locally-free-has-norm), 0BCY (divisors-lemma-norm-invertible, Norm_f(f^*L) is L^{tensor d}), and 0BCZ (divisors-lemma-norm-map-invertible), for a section of the nth tensor power.

proof.text:
Choose the maps $
u_V$ supplied by [lem-sfb-finite-locally-free-function-norm]. Choose an open cover $(V_i)$ trivializing $L$, with generators $e_i$ and units $a_{ij}$ satisfying $e_i=a_{ij}e_j$. Put $M=f^*L$ and $E_i=f^*e_i$ on $f^{-1}V_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor] and the local trivialization clause of [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-invertible], $M$ is invertible and the $E_i$ are generators (pull back the trivializations and use $\mathcal O_Y\otimes_{f^{-1}\mathcal O_X}f^{-1}\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_Y$). The pullback definition gives $E_i=(f^\sharp a_{ij})E_j$. Apply [lem-sfb-norm-frame-tensor-section-gluing] to this cover, $M,E_i,
u$. It gives an invertible module $N$ with generators $F_i$ and $F_i=
u(f^\sharp a_{ij})F_j=a_{ij}^dF_j$, and for our given $s$ a section $t_N\in\Gamma(X,N^{\otimes n})$ with $t_N|_{V_i}=
u_{V_i}(b_i)F_i^{\otimes n}$, where $s|_{f^{-1}V_i}=b_iE_i^{\otimes n}$.

proof.text: Identify $N^{\otimes n}$ with $L^{\otimes(dn)}$ explicitly. The source has local generators $F_i^{\otimes n}$ with transition $(a_{ij}^d)^n=a_{ij}^{dn}$ by [lem-sfb-norm-frame-tensor-section-gluing]. The target has generators $e_i^{\otimes(dn)}$ with the same transitions: restriction commutes with iterated tensor products by [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-tensor-comparison], so iterated tensor products of the trivialization $L|_{V_i}\cong\mathcal O_{V_i}$, the tensor unitor and associator in [lem-weil-pbc-module-tensor-symmetric-monoidal] give these generators, and bilinearity gives $e_i^{\otimes(dn)}=a_{ij}^{dn}e_j^{\otimes(dn)}$. Therefore the local linear maps $F_i^{\otimes n}\mapsto e_i^{\otimes(dn)}$ agree on overlaps. Glue them and their local inverses using clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules]. Their composites are identities locally and hence globally by the same clause. Let $t$ be the image of $t_N$; its local formula is $t|_{V_i}=\nu_{V_i}(b_i)e_i^{\otimes(dn)}$.

proof.text:
For $x\in V_i$, the local formula for $t$ and the fact that $e_i^{\otimes(dn)}$ is a generator give $x\in X_t\iff
u_{V_i}(b_i)(x)
e0$. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-function-norm-nonvanishing] with $p=f$, $V=V_i$ and $b=b_i$: finiteness is part of finite local freeness, and all its multiplicativity, restriction and vanishing hypotheses hold by step 1. Thus this is equivalent to every $y\in f^{-1}(\{x\})$ satisfying $b_i(y)
e0$. Since $E_i^{\otimes n}$ is a generator, the last condition is exactly $f^{-1}(\{x\})\subseteq Y_s$, using the residue-field definition of the nonvanishing opens in [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. The $V_i$ cover $X$, proving the asserted fibre description.

proof.text: For every $x\in X$, $f^{-1}(\{x\})\subseteq Y_s$ means that there is no $y\in Y\setminus Y_s$ with $f(y)=x$. This is precisely $x\notin f(Y\setminus Y_s)$. Taking sets gives the second displayed equality.

Step 4 is an elementary set identity. There is no cycle (closure of 201 nodes), no SGA, and no re-split note. The null from.node is inherited from the null parent.
